result.summary: Review of target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 (feature/binary-config-serve-20260930) in scope 'server resource acquisition, readiness/mutation gate, startup abort, bind-failure reverse cleanup'. Verdict FINDINGS: 1 MEDIUM (reproduced) + 3 LOW. The ordered acquisition/rollback design is correct on every advertised path - I traced and probed pre-abort, lock contention, instance-owner mismatch, recovery failure, API bind failure, metrics bind failure, abort during recovery, abort during first provisioning, and idempotent stop; no lock, SQLite handle or listener leak in any. F1 MEDIUM: src/serve.ts:193 registers the raw eventLogger flush in setInterval with no guard, so any fs fault on <DB_PATH>.log (EISDIR/ENOSPC/EACCES/EROFS) kills the process via an uncaught exception, bypassing release() entirely - gate not closed, listeners not stopped, database not closed, lock not unlinked, no final flush, message not redacted. Reproduced: probe seeded a queued worker with FakeProvider, put a directory at <db>.log, and the process died with UNCAUGHT EISDIR while /health was 200 a moment earlier. Only the one-shot final flush has the try/finally; tests/serve.test.ts never exercises a failing flush (20/20 pass). F2 LOW: /health returns 200 for the whole first provisioning pass while every mutation is 503 (up to ~2 min by default; already asserted by tests/serve.test.ts:432). F3 LOW: src/serve.ts:141-142 clears the log interval before closing the gate, the reverse of docs/SERVE.md:48. F4 LOW: a second SIGINT/SIGTERM is swallowed (serve-command.ts:112); probed to confirm the deadline still forces exit 70. Artifacts: /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/review.md and findings.json; logs under /workspace/.swarmforge/logs. /workspace/repo left clean at assigned baseline 5672ead.
result.details:
Target verified in a disposable detached clone at /tmp/rev-17/target (git rev-parse HEAD = d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895); /workspace/repo was left on the assigned branch at 5672ead, clean and unmodified. No source changes, commits, pushes, merges, tags, releases or config changes were made.

Scope reviewed: src/serve.ts, src/serve-command.ts, src/main.ts, the cli.ts serve path, the coordinator surface startServer depends on (recover, startProvisioning, stop, track/idle at src/coordinator.ts:255-300, 358-359, 807-814), src/runtime.ts (acquireProcessLock:145-171, eventLogger:172-212), src/http.ts, config.ts port/host superRefine, docs/SERVE.md, tests/serve.test.ts and tests/fixtures/serve-command-child.ts.

F1 (MEDIUM, reproduced) - src/serve.ts:193 `logTimer = setInterval(flush, 1000)`. Only the single final flush is protected (try/finally at 148-156); the periodic callback is unguarded, and eventLogger writes the store and the filesystem directly so it is outside the coordinator drain. Trigger: any fs error while events are pending. Consequence: uncaught exception, abrupt exit outside release(), raw unredacted message. Reproduction: /tmp/rev-17/probes/logflush2.ts (seed a queued worker with the repo FakeProvider/FakeAgent, mkdir at <db>.log, startServer) -> UNCAUGHT EISDIR, probe exit 42, server was healthy before. Control probe logflush.ts (same target, no pending events) exits 0. Fix: wrap the interval callback in try/catch and report through the redacted path, or route a fatal event-log fault through the idempotent shutdown().

F2 (LOW) - the gate is a mutation gate only, so /health is 200 from the listener bind (serve.ts:170-191) to gate.open() (203), i.e. the whole first startProvisioning() (194). Existing test tests/serve.test.ts:432 already pins {mutation:503, health:200}. Window can be ~2 min by default (MAX_PROVISIONING 4 x API_TIMEOUT_MS 30s, coordinator.ts:41-59,457). Fix: separate readiness from liveness, or open the gate before the first tick.

F3 (LOW) - code order (clearInterval at 141, then gate.close() at 142) contradicts docs/SERVE.md:48. Cosmetic today; swap the statements or fix the doc.

F4 (LOW) - serve-command.ts:112 `if (requested) return;` ignores every later signal. Probed via /tmp/rev-17/probes/signal-matrix.ts against the repo's own blocked child fixture with a 400ms deadline: one SIGTERM, SIGTERM twice, and SIGTERM+SIGINT all exit 70 at the deadline with durable state intact. Correct per the documented contract; reported only as an operational sharp edge (no in-process escalation for an operator).

Also checked and found clean: the src/serve.ts:199-205 abort window is not a lost-abort race (no await between the aborted check and addEventListener); withAbort attaches both handlers so no unhandled rejection; the idle drain cannot spin; shutdown() memoisation makes double release impossible; the HTTP surface is POST-only for MCP so GET/HEAD/OPTIONS are genuinely read-only; config validation rejects metrics-port == port; and both entry points (main.ts, cli.ts:191-205) import serve-command only after settings resolve, so a rejected config acquires nothing.

Limitations: only tests/serve.test.ts plus tsc --noEmit were executed (full suite and biome are out of scope for a single reviewer); F1's ENOSPC/EACCES variants are code-evidenced rather than reproduced; startup-abort timing was assessed by trace plus the repo's own blocking-provider tests; no real provider, model endpoint or infrastructure was contacted and no real credentials appear in any output. Reviewer probes live only in /tmp/rev-17/probes.

result.followup_reason: One actionable MEDIUM finding: src/serve.ts:193 registers the event-log flush in setInterval without error handling, so any filesystem fault on <DB_PATH>.log (reproduced as EISDIR) terminates the process through an uncaught exception instead of the ordered release - gate left open, listeners not stopped, SQLite not closed, lock not unlinked, no final flush, and an unredacted error message. Fix by wrapping the interval callback in try/catch and reporting through commandRedactor, or by routing a fatal event-log fault through the already idempotent shutdown(). Three LOW items (readiness indistinguishable from liveness during the first provisioning pass; shutdown order contradicting docs/SERVE.md:48; a swallowed second termination signal) are also worth a follow-up decision.
